description:
**Blocked by d06.1 (VDom core must exist). Read the deck §11
"Reconciler: pure state, no GenServer" and §13 "Worked example:
streaming Markdown" before starting.**

The reconciler is **not** a GenServer. It is a pure functional
module over an immutable `%UI.State{}` value. Interactive's existing
GenServer drives the loop unchanged; the only addition is calling
the new pure functions and using `next_wait_ms/1` to pick its
GenServer-timeout. RenderLoop is unchanged.

**Read first:**
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex` — the GenServer
  this work integrates with. Pay attention to its existing receive
  loop, `handle_event/2` chain, and `send_render/1`. The integration
  surface is small (replace the body of `send_render` and the
  `handle_info` clauses that today call it inline).
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_loop.ex` — the
  downstream Task that owns Renderer; receives
  `{:render, lines, cursor_seq}` messages. Don't change it.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/key.ex` — Key struct shape.
- The new VDom modules from d06.1.

**New modules (suggested layout):**
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/ui/state.ex` — the pure
  reconciler value + functions.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/ui/hooks.ex` — `use_state/2`,
  `use_memo/2`, `use_frame/2`, `use_key/3`, `use_effect/3`. Hook
  handle is the second argument; first argument is the state value;
  return shape varies per hook.

**`%UI.State{}` API (every function pure):**

  * `new(root_component, props) :: state`
  * `handle_key(state, %Key{}) :: state` — fold key event through
    active `use_key` subscriptions; setter calls produce a new
    state value.
  * `handle_event(state, term) :: state` — same for arbitrary
    messages routed to a hole (streaming snapshots, tool deltas,
    custom timer wakeups).
  * `tick(state, now_ms) :: state` — advance frame clock; flag
    cells whose `use_frame` deadline has passed as needing
    re-render.
  * `paint(state, %RenderContext{}) :: {state, iodata, cursor_or_nil}` —
    single-pass paint (delegates to `OctoPi.TUI.VDom.Paint.paint/3`
    from d06.1). Returns updated state (memo cache, hook-cell GC,
    cleared invalidated set, updated last_paint_at_ms) plus the
    bytes the renderer will diff plus an optional cursor.
  * `dirty?(state) :: boolean` — has any cell been invalidated
    since the last paint?
  * `next_wait_ms(state) :: non_neg_integer() | :infinity` —
    earliest pending deadline expressed in ms-from-now. Aggregates:
    (a) animation deadlines from active `use_frame` cells;
    (b) the max-staleness cap (`dirty_since_ms + max_staleness_ms`,
    default `max_staleness_ms = 16`) which prevents paint
    starvation under continuous event pressure.

**Hook semantics (contracts from d06.1, tests live here):**

  - Hook handle `h` carries a reference to the hole's cell within
    the state value. The cell is keyed by hole id (stable identity
    assigned by the parent VHole).
  - Hook-cell values are stored by identity, never deep-compared.
    Setter is the only "changed" signal. Test: storing a struct
    with identical fields but allocated at different points reads
    as different.
  - Setters called during render fold into the same paint pass.
    Test: a render function that calls its setter once produces
    one paint, not two; the new value is reflected in this paint's
    output.
  - Hook-cell GC: cells not visited during a paint are retained
    one frame, then dropped. Implement as a generation counter on
    the state value; no GenServer timers.

**Hook implementations:**

  - `use_state(h, init_or_thunk) :: {value, setter}` — setter is
    a 2-arity function `(state, new_value) -> state` (or 1-arity
    closure that takes only state if you've curried — pick one and
    document it).
  - `use_memo(h, key, thunk) :: vnode` — the only public way to
    build a `%VMemo{}` for a hook-cell-bound subtree. Memo cache
    survives across paints; eviction follows hook-cell GC.
  - `use_frame(h, ms) :: frame_index` — registers an animation
    deadline; cell becomes due `ms` after the last visit. Returns
    the current frame index (a monotonic non_neg_integer) so
    components can derive animation phase deterministically.
  - `use_key(h, key_spec, handler) :: :ok` — subscribes to keyboard
    events. `key_spec` matches `%Key{key, modifiers}` shape. Handler
    is a 1-arity function `(state) -> state`.
  - `use_effect(h, key, fn -> cleanup_or_nil end) :: :ok` — runs
    on mount and when `key` changes; cleanup runs on unmount or key
    change.

**Interactive integration: mailbox-drain + dirty + debounced paint.**

State-mutating handlers in `interactive.ex` (`:hid`, `:stream_delta`,
`:bash_done`, etc.) fold the event into UI.State and reschedule:

```elixir
@debounce_ms 4

def handle_info({:hid, key}, state) do
  ui = UI.State.handle_key(state.ui, key)
  reschedule(%{state | ui: ui})
end

defp reschedule(state) do
  wait =
    if UI.State.dirty?(state.ui) do
      min(@debounce_ms, UI.State.next_wait_ms(state.ui))
    else
      UI.State.next_wait_ms(state.ui)
    end
  {:noreply, state, wait}
end

def handle_info(:timeout, state) do
  now = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
  ui  = UI.State.tick(state.ui, now)

  state =
    if UI.State.dirty?(ui) do
      {ui, iodata, cursor} = UI.State.paint(ui, render_ctx(state))
      send(state.render_loop, {:render, to_lines(iodata), build_cursor_seq(cursor)})
      %{state | ui: ui}
    else
      %{state | ui: ui}
    end

  {:noreply, state, UI.State.next_wait_ms(state.ui)}
end
```

The GenServer's "timeout fires only when the mailbox is empty"
semantics give us free burst coalescing: 12 streaming deltas
arriving back-to-back become 1 paint. The max-staleness cap inside
`next_wait_ms/1` prevents starvation under continuous event
pressure.

This matches the `{:noreply, state, ms}` pattern called out in
the `feedback_genserver_timeout` memory: one pending timeout,
sorted-deadline aggregation lives inside `UI.State`, no
`Process.send_after` fan-out.

**Acceptance:**
- Pure-function tests over `UI.State` (no GenServer involvement
  in the test process):
  * Feed a key sequence, assert the resulting state's painted
    bytes.
  * Assert `next_wait_ms` coalesces correctly across multiple
    animated holes (smallest deadline wins).
  * Assert memo invalidation on hook-state change triggers a
    repaint of just the affected subtree (sibling memos stay
    cached).
  * Assert `dirty?/1` flips false → true on setter call, true →
    false after `paint`.
  * Assert max-staleness bound: a state continuously
    re-invalidated at 1ms intervals still gets painted within
    `dirty_since_ms + max_staleness_ms` (within one max_staleness
    window).
  * Assert hook-cell GC: a hole that disappears from the tree has
    its cell dropped after one frame of absence.
  * Assert render-time setter folding: a render fn that calls
    its setter does not produce a second paint scheduling.
- Integration test against `Interactive`: simulate a 12-event
  burst at <1ms intervals; assert RenderLoop receives exactly one
  `{:render, _, _}` message.
- No `Process.sleep` in any test — sync via telemetry events
  (`[:octo_pi_tui, :vdom, :paint]`) or explicit time injection.
title: Reconciler state + hooks (pure functions; Interactive drives the loop)
